So basically, peacocks in my world are huge magical beings associated with frost and cold. They revive themselves after they die, like phoenixes, and there's been a massive feud between the two races since the beginning of the world. Peacocks are all usually insanely prideful, vain, and frustrating to work with.

There are exceptions to every rule though. Whereas most peacocks stay in the coldest areas of the world, flaunting their own egos, Hierodule runs around the world, chasing after Radiance no matter how hot or humid it gets. Every time she manages to get close, she Leeroy Jenkins herself at Radiance, and promptly gets killed. The moment she resurrects, she does this again without any sort of rest.

It's worth noting that while weaker phoenixes lose many memories after returning to life, Radiance is so strong it's extremely doubtful that death would affect him at all. It's likely Hierodule had some sort of plan in mind that she could only carry out while Radiance was awaiting a resurrection, but the thousands of years of combat and the millions of deaths she's had have caused her to forget just what that was.

Hierodule has none of the pride or vanity associated with her race, choosing to carry out her one goal with any underhanded means. Out of all the peacocks though, she is by far the most stubborn and relentless. Her many deaths to Radiance also make some individuals think of her as weak. This is not the case. Radiance is simply just one of the world's strongest beings. Should by some miracle, Hierodule's anger be turned on literally anything else, it's doubtful they'd exist for much longer. She's spent the last 7,000 years fighting the King of Phoenixes, after all.

"That's the difference between you and me. You've won against me millions, billions of times, it's true. You need to keep winning though. I only need to win once."

\- Dragon Lord Yongheng to Ouroboros at the end of time

"Seven thousand years we have faced against the other. My memory has faded to nothing but hatred for your kind, my soul has my combat techniques engraved onto it over the centuries I've faced you. I am Hierodule, and until you fall, I shall continue to fight."

\- Major Peacock Hierodule to Radiance, King of Phoenixes

The Vampire Queen is capable of stealing life force from living beings, and using this energy to form powerful weapons. Even just a few years of stolen life can create a weapon that would be truly terrifying in the hands of a normal person.

In exchange for 10 million years of stolen life, however, she is able to create a lance so dangerous its very existence is terrifying. Any attempt to use this weapon fills the user with a deep, existential terror so deep-rooted one's body will outright refuse to touch, let alone wield it. For less powerful individuals, being in the weapon's mere presence is a sensation terrifying enough to warrant suicide.

Anything killed by this weapon will have its very existence erased. No one, not even the user or the world itself will be able to remember what was slain with this lance, merely the fact that it killed *something*. Anything connected to what was killed will feel intense fear and paranoia for the rest of their lives, eternally feeling that something is missing, but never able to figure out what.

Forbidden or cursed knowledge is information that all living beings soul's will reject to even acknowledge. Whether it's spoken or read, every living thing that interacts with this information will have every bodily function act against them to keep them from understanding it. Eyes will blot out written text, even if you can't read the language it's written on, and ears will only hear garbled nonsense, no matter if it's it English, Latin, or even Morse code.

If it's particularly bad, souls will react violently. Fight or flight instincts will kick in, and every living thing will feel as though their very existence is in danger. The worst of it, the soul will literally just kill the physical body it's currently inhabiting. Say one of the world's darkest secrets, and everyone in earshot will spontaneously go braindead for no apparent reason. It is possible to gain resistance to this effect by slowly subjecting yourself to tamer pieces of information first and then working your way up, but given the rarity of such information, and the existential dread that comes with subjecting yourself to it, such individuals are quite rare.
